# Toyotama: the stories first, then the spelling

You cannot weigh an accent without knowing what it carries. Here is what **Toyotama** has been carrying.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Bride of the Sea Palace.** Hoori — Hikohohodemi-no-mikoto, the hunter prince — came to the seashore weeping over a lost fishhook and a broken brotherhood.  Guided by the old man of the sea, Shihotsuchi, he descended to the palace of Watatsumi, the dragon god of the depths.  The palace walls were fish-scaled, its lanes alive with every creature of the sea, and the god received the prince with ceremony, presenting him to his daughter Toyotama-hime: 'I give you this maiden; dwell in our midst as long as heaven endures.

**The Vow at the Birth-Hut.** When Toyotama was with child, she told Hoori: 'In our country, when our kind give birth, we do so in our true form; do not look. ' She built a parturition hut, sealed its entry, and withdrew.  But longing overcame the prince: he stole to the hut and peered inside, and there he saw no woman but a great eight-fathom sea-dragon — a wani, sea-serpent or crocodile — coiling about the child.

**Tamayori Raises the Child.** Toyotama did not leave the child wholly orphaned.  From the sea palace she sent her younger sister, Tamayori-hime — 'the jewel-adorning princess' — to nurse the boy at the shore.  The Kojiki names him Ugayafukiaezu, 'he of the unfinished roof': when the birth-hut was built, its thatching was left incomplete, and the name fixed the broken moment in the child himself.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **豊玉毘売命**, as Kojiki, Hikohohodemi-no-mikoto and Toyotama-hime cycle; trans. Donald L. Philippi, Kojiki (Princeton University Press, 1969) and Nihon Shoki (Nihongi), Age of the Gods volumes, parallel variants; trans. W. G. Aston (1896) record. The name means "Abundant jewel".


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Toyotama
- **ASCII form:** toyotama
- **Meaning:** "Abundant jewel"
- **Domain of influence:** Sea, Mother of Jimmu
- **Pantheon:** Japanese
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** 豊玉毘売命
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 494 of 546

## The Name Travels

Toyotama belongs to one of the oldest families of tales in East Asia: the supernatural bride whose true form must not be seen — the Japanese cousin of the Chinese dragon-palace romances and of the hagoromo 'feather-robe' cycle, in which a wife recovers her stolen robe and leaves her human family.  Buddhist Japan read her father's palace through the nāga lens: the fish-scaled halls of the deep are the sea-serpents' treasure house, and Ryūjin's daughter moves between the two cosmologies without friction.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Toyotama** stands at [/toyotama/](/toyotama/) — [lore](/toyotama/lore/), [scholars](/toyotama/scholars/), [patterns](/toyotama/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. Tier-2 here means one preserved truth — not less important, just singular. The temple shows it and names it.
